{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Collaborative Research, Development and Commercialization Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel)
**Re:** Playbook review — RevMed collaboration agreement (we represent Sanofi, the Customer)
**Status of review:** Complete except for one rule requiring manual completion (see Next steps)

---

## Executive summary

The agreement is, on balance, favourable to us. The licence grant, IP ownership architecture, assignment rights, termination-for-convenience right and audit mechanics all meet or comfortably exceed our playbook positions, and we found no exclusivity, minimum-commitment, MFN, non-solicit, liquidated-damages or auto-renewal terms burdening us. Governing law is New York with JAMS arbitration and appropriate court carve-outs, which satisfies the rule on its material terms.

Two issues warrant redlines, both critical:

1. **No IP infringement indemnity from RevMed (Section 14.1).** The indemnity covers negligence, breach of representations and breach of obligations, but contains no head for third-party claims that the licensed technology or the Products infringe or misappropriate third-party IP. That risk is only reached indirectly through the Article XIII IP warranties, which are largely knowledge-qualified and given only as of the Execution Date, while Section 14.2(a) affirmatively places third-party claims arising from our Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization on us and Section 10.7 gives us only a first right to negotiate a third-party licence at our own cost. This fails the fallback.

2. **No monetary liability cap (Section 14.5).** Section 14.5 is the only limitation-of-liability provision; it waives indirect and consequential damages and preserves the indemnity, confidentiality and IP carve-outs, but contains no cap of any kind. Both Parties' direct-damages exposure is unlimited, which fails the fallback requirement of a mutual cap of at least twelve months' fees. As the paying party, a mutual cap is materially in our interest.

Separately, a number of commercial numerals are redacted ([***]) in this copy — termination notice periods, audit frequency and thresholds, arbitral seat and arbitrator count, transition durations, and the Section 10.1(a) ownership allocation. Each should be confirmed against the unredacted execution version.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (§ 14.1, 14.2(a), 14.3, 14.5; cf. § 10.7, Art. XIII) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (§ 14.5; cf. § 14.6) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant (fallback on joint ownership) | Intellectual Property Rights (§ 3.2, 3.4, 3.6, 6.2, 6.5, 10.1(a), 10.4(c), 10.5, 12.3(c)(ii)C) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | General Provisions (§ 15.2; cf. § 12.2(b)–(e), 12.3(c), 9.7(a)) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | License (§ 3.1(a), 3.4; § 15.2(a)(ii)) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | License (§ 3.1, 13.2(q); Art. VII, § 7.2, 7.3; cf. § 12.2(d)) |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | Term and Termination (§ 12.2(a)(i), 12.2(b)–(e), 12.3(c)) |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | Financial Provisions (Art. IX, § 9.6; § 12.2(a)(i), 12.3(c)(ii)C, 12.6) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Needs review (verification failed)** | Not determined |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Financial Provisions (§ 9.8, 9.9) |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions (§ 15.5, 15.6(a), (f), (h)–(j)) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant (fallback) | § 13.3 Covenants by RevMed (with § 4.2(b), 5.2(b), 13.2, 13.4(b), 13.5, 7.3) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Compliant | Confidentiality; Publication (§ 11.6; with § 12.3, 12.4, 7.2) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Manufacturing and Supply (Art. VII, § 7.3; cf. Art. IX, § 5.7) |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant (none present) | Manufacturing and Supply (§ 7.3; Financial Provisions) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant (none present) | General Provisions |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant (not applicable) | Term and Termination |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant (fallback) | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (§ 14.6) |

---

## Redlines we are proposing

**1. Section 14.1 — add an IP infringement head of indemnity.** We propose a minimal addition as new Section 14.1(d) covering third-party claims that the licensed technology or the Products infringe or misappropriate third-party IP, leaving RevMed's existing carve-outs for our own negligence and breaches intact. Our own indemnity in Section 14.2 is otherwise appropriately confined to our development and commercialization conduct and our breaches, and we are not seeking to narrow it.

**2. Section 14.5 — add a mutual aggregate cap.** We propose a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' payments and USD 1,000,000, keeping the existing indemnification, confidentiality and IP carve-outs outside the cap and adding gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud, and confirming that Sanofi's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

---

## Walk-away items

On the findings before us, **no walk-away trigger is engaged**. Specifically:

- **Audit (§ 9.9):** no right of direct or remote access to our systems and no unannounced or unlimited audit right — walk-away territory is not engaged.
- **Governing law / venue (§ 15.5, 15.6):** New York law with JAMS arbitration in English; not vendor home-jurisdiction law and not arbitration seated abroad.
- **Warranty (Art. XIII):** Section 13.5 opens with "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS ARTICLE XIII," preserving RevMed's express warranties — the opposite of an "AS IS / all warranties disclaimed" position.
- **Transition (§ 11.6):** mutual return-or-destruction with written certification and archival carve-outs; not an immediate-deletion regime.
- **Insurance (§ 14.6):** insurance is in place, and the walk-away scenario (no insurance where a vendor processes personal data or works on-site) does not arise because RevMed is a licensor/co-development counterparty rather than a hosting vendor.

The two critical deviations above are deviations from the fallback, not walk-away items, and we expect both to be resolvable.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the two redlines** to Sections 14.1 and 14.5 in our first turn, framed as the fallback positions rather than opening asks.
2. **Complete the non-compete review (NONCOMPETE).** This rule could not be verified — the automated pass failed after exceeding its tool iteration limit — and requires a manual read of the restrictive-covenant and licence provisions before we sign off.
3. **Confirm redacted numerals against the unredacted execution version**, in particular: the Section 12.2(a)(i) convenience-notice periods; the Section 9.9 audit notice, frequency and underpayment percentage (whether these sit at 30 days/5% or 15 days/10%); the Section 15.6(a) arbitral seat and number of arbitrators (we want a U.S. seat, ideally New York, New York); the Section 12.3 transition durations (we are looking for a 90-day/6-month floor); and the Section 10.1(a) ownership allocation.
4. **Revisit the IP finding if Section 10.1(a) reads differently unredacted.** Our compliant classification assumes the sole/joint split follows the defined terms; if the unredacted text allocated Sanofi-generated inventions to RevMed we would reopen it.
5. **Track two items for the Supply and Quality Agreements under Section 7.3:** secure an express batch conformance warranty (GMP, specifications, no adulteration) with replacement-or-refund remedies, and confirm Section 13.5 is not read to reach warranties given in those ancillary agreements.
6. **Note for survival:** Section 7.2 (manufacturing know-how transfer) is not listed in the Section 12.4 survival list, so post-expiry manufacturing know-how support is not expressly preserved. We can raise this as a low-cost cleanup alongside the two substantive redlines."}
